summary: Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Mahidol University by 2021 under doctoral supervisors Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.
Enga Teramoto (1872–1940) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Kyoto University as a lecturer and became a professor at Otani University in 1915.
Enichi Ocho (1906–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1926 to 1929. He later served as professor emeritus at Otani University.
Enryo Inoue (1858–1919) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1881–1885). He founded Toyo University, serving there from circa 1887 to 1906.

Ensho Kanakura (1896–1987) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy after studying at the University of Tokyo (~1917–1920). He was a professor at Tohoku University and Rissho University, and a member of the Japan Academy.
Ensho Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University (attested 1996) under the doctoral supervision of Eshō Mikogami.

Enshu Kurumiya (b. 1942) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the Australian National University by 1974 and served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He earned a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London and held posts at the University of Milan (~1994–2002) and the University of Bologna (~2002–2016).

Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under the doctoral supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton.
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under the doctoral supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Manchester (~1951–1958). He held posts at Manchester, Lancaster University, and the University of Sydney as First Chair of Religious Studies (1977–1996).

Eric M. Greene is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from UC Berkeley by 2012 under Robert H. Sharf. In 2017, he was an assistant professor of religious studies at Yale University.
Eric Reinders is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied under mentors Allan G. Grapard and William F. Powell.

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia, completing doctoral work under Paul Groner (attested 2012).

Erich Frauwallner (1898–1974) was an Austrian scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna (1918–1921), later serving there as professor and founding the Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens in 1957.

Erich Haenisch (1880–1966) specialized in sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held professorships at Leipzig University (~1925–1932), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932–1945), and the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1946–1952).
Erich Rudolf Jaensch (1883–1940) was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who held academic posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1912–1913) and the University of Marburg (~1913–1940).
Erik Braun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Janet Gyatso.

Erik Haarh (1929–1993) was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who earned a doctor's degree at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1969) and held a post at the Royal Danish Library (~1953–1974).

Erik J. Hammerstrom is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD from Indiana University and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).
